proof.title: E. Hendren, A computer-assisted proof of optimality for Heilbronn's problem with ten points in a triangle, Zenodo (November 2026)

coordinates_source.ref: David Cantrell's original coordinates (Mathematica list), received September 2026
coordinates_source.note: Original author's arrangement for the entry, previously shown only as a reconstruction; Cantrell's literals converge to the same configuration under local polishing. Coordinates refined by Ethan Hendren, November 2026: exact refinement to the local maximum, the certified unique solution of the tie system (+7.5e-15); github.com/NERD-NEH007/heilbronn-discovery-lab.

changelog.text: computer-assisted proof of optimality by Ethan Hendren: the known configuration (David Cantrell, June 2007) is optimal and unique up to symmetry, with value 0.0433767406780570017601...; an affine normalization to eight contact families, an exact cell-graph search and exactly checked certificates, with a certified second-order basin around the optimum; every split and closure, 16,166 shards and 92,003,233 closures, is replayed in exact arithmetic by a separate checker that does not use the search code; trace, checker and release receipt archived on Zenodo; AI-assisted, and so far replayed only by its author
